clue.text: Conservative in agreement about local war memorial

indicators.note: about here means turned round, so the phrase for being in agreement is read backwards

parts.note: to be in agreement is to be at one
a local is a British pub, abbreviated PH for public house

explanation.surface: A Tory finds himself agreeing with a plan for the village war memorial.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' looks like 'concerning' but turns ATONE round; 'local' is British slang for the neighbourhood pub.
explanation.definitionFit: A monument to the war dead whose bodies lie elsewhere, such as the one in Whitehall.

clue.text: He supports Tiger Woods, perhaps, as rat gets punch

parts.note: a rat is a scoundrel, a cad
a die is a punch or stamp used to cut or shape metal

explanation.surface: A golfer's helper is portrayed as a rat who gets punched.
explanation.walkthrough: 'punch' looks like a blow but is the metalworking tool.
explanation.definitionFit: A golf bag carrier assists a player such as Tiger Woods on the course.

clue.text: Almost new potato

parts.note: an early is a new-season potato variety, as in Jersey earlies

explanation.surface: Something is very nearly a new potato.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words mean not quite, just short of completely.

clue.text: Start to think everyone's Conservative? It's hard to believe

indicators.note: the start of the word think supplies its opening letter

parts.note: everyone is all, and everyone's gives all's
a Tory is a member of the UK Conservative Party

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether everybody has become a Tory, which seems incredible.
explanation.definitionFit: An exaggerated or unlikely tale is something hard to credit.

clue.text: Dad getting chased by goatsucker ruined the holidays

indicators.note: being chased means having something come behind, so the father's word comes first

parts.note: pa is an informal word for dad

indicators.note: ruined signals that the letters of goatsucker are wrecked and rearranged

explanation.surface: Father is pursued by a nightjar and the family break is spoiled.
explanation.walkthrough: A goatsucker is another name for the nightjar bird; 'ruined' scrambles it to CKAGETOURS, and 'getting chased by' puts Dad in front.
explanation.definitionFit: Ready-made holiday packages with travel and hotel bundled are the holidays in question.

clue.text: Short form of county match regularly provokes passion

parts.note: Warwickshire, an English county, is cut short to its first three letters

indicators.note: taking letters at regular intervals from match picks every other one

explanation.surface: A county cricket game regularly stirs strong feelings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' takes M, T, H from match.
explanation.definitionFit: Warmth is ardour or fervour, a strength of feeling akin to passion.

clue.text: Segregation barred chap — one had, in short, to be separate

indicators.note: barred means excluded, so these letters are taken away

parts.note: apartheid was the system of racial segregation in South Africa
a chap is a he
I is the Roman numeral one
had is shortened to 'd as in I'd

explanation.surface: A system of segregation kept men out, one had to be kept apart.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove HE, I and D from APARTHEID to leave the answer; 'to be' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Apart describes things held away from each other, distinct and divided.

clue.text: Student enthralled by changing climate of Mercury?

indicators.note: being enthralled by something is being held within it
changing tells us the letters of climate are rearranged

parts.note: L is a learner, the student driver's plate

explanation.surface: A student is fascinated by the shifting climate on the planet Mercury.
explanation.walkthrough: 'changing' makes METALIC from CLIMATE, and L goes inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Mercury is a metal, so something of mercury is metal-like in nature.

clue.text: Flourished once, during opening of present era

indicators.note: during places one thing in the middle of another

parts.note: a hole is an opening

indicators.note: flourished as in brandished or waved about, so the letters of once are shaken up

explanation.surface: Something thrived once, at the start of the present age.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flourished' tempts as the definition, meaning thrived, but it is the scrambling signal (waved about) giving OCEN; 'during' sets that inside the opening. The Holocene is the current geological epoch.
explanation.definitionFit: The geological epoch of the last twelve thousand years or so is the current era.

clue.text: Inability to make progress, having gone to Yale?

definitions.meaning: a stalemate where neither side can move forward
Yale is a lock maker, so a lock that has gone dead

explanation.surface: Someone's career stalls after going to an Ivy League university.
explanation.walkthrough: Yale looks like the university, but it is the brand of door lock.
explanation.definitionFit: A standstill in negotiation where nobody can advance is a stalemate.

clue.text: Hilary's husband allowed to retire

parts.note: a man is a husband, as in man and wife

indicators.note: to retire is to withdraw backwards, so the word is read in reverse

parts.note: to let is to allow

explanation.surface: A woman's husband is permitted to stop working.
explanation.walkthrough: Hilary Mantel was the novelist of Wolf Hall; 'to retire' turns LET into TEL.
explanation.definitionFit: The surname of novelist Hilary Mantel, so the clue's possessive supplies her family name.

clue.text: Try to fell the god of pastures and fail miserably

parts.note: to have a go is to try
to fell is to bring down
taken as written
Pan is the Greek god of shepherds and pastures

explanation.surface: An attempt to topple a Greek nature god goes badly.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom for being wasted or collapsing utterly, as if flushed away.

clue.text: Paid less, nurse doesn't work hard

explanation.surface: Being on lower pay, a nurse slacks off.

explanation.definitionFit: To idle is to laze rather than labour, so this is the third-person verb.

clue.text: Unholy topic also concerning Pope

indicators.note: unholy suggests something messed up, so the letters of topic and also are jumbled

explanation.walkthrough: 'Unholy' rearranges TOPIC ALSO.
explanation.definitionFit: Apostolic relates to the Pope as successor of the apostle Peter.

clue.text: Advantageous placement for Eastern European?

parts.note: the front spot on a racing grid, read as a place given to someone from Poland

explanation.surface: Where should a person from Poland be put for the best advantage?
explanation.definitionFit: In motor racing the front starting spot on the grid is the most favourable.

clue.text: One poxy beer ain't making you drunk

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: poxy means rotten or rubbish, so the letters of beer and ain't are scrambled

explanation.surface: One rubbish beer isn't going to get you drunk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'poxy' rearranges BEERAINT into NEBRIATE, after I. 'making you' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: An inebriate is a drunkard, someone habitually intoxicated.

clue.text: Ought little person to meet a jerk like Albert Herring?

parts.note: ought is a variant of nought, so O
per is a shortening of person
a tic is a jerky involuntary movement

explanation.surface: Should a small person meet a fool such as Albert Herring?
explanation.walkthrough: Albert Herring is a comic opera by Benjamin Britten; 'jerk' looks like a fool.
explanation.definitionFit: Albert Herring is a Britten opera, so the question asks what kind of work it is.

clue.text: Instruments show gases and particles

parts.note: Cl is the symbol for the gas chlorine
Ar is the symbol for the gas argon
ions are charged particles

explanation.surface: Musical instruments display gases and particles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gases' gives two chemical symbols at once; 'show' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Clarions are shrill medieval trumpets, a kind of brass instrument.

clue.text: Harassment of poet by lonely Guardian columnist

indicators.note: harassment disturbs the letters of poet by lonely so they rearrange

explanation.surface: A newspaper writer is harassed by a solitary poet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Harassment of' rearranges POET BY LONELY.
explanation.definitionFit: A well-known writer of opinion pieces for the Guardian newspaper since 1998.

clue.text: 12 could be a double whammy

definitions.meaning: the number 12 written out digit by digit
a boxer's quick pair of punches, left then right

explanation.definitionFit: A combination of two blows in quick succession, like a jab followed by a cross.

clue.text: Law of French-Canadian natives

parts.note: de is French for of
the Cree are an indigenous people of Canada

explanation.definitionFit: A decree is an official order having the force of law.

clue.text: Metal bats rather grabbing attention

clue.text: Hobbema illustration's secret message

indicators.note: secret means kept out of sight, so the answer is tucked in these words

explanation.definitionFit: An electronic message sent over the internet.

clue.text: Scrubbing grand country house Aga?

parts.note: a grange is a country house with farm buildings

clue.text: Scandinavian blade cut part of body

parts.note: Thor is the Norse god of thunder

indicators.note: cut means trimmed, so the final letter goes

explanation.walkthrough: 'cut' docks the E of AXE.

clue.text: Make a mess of second page, second of two

parts.note: the latter is the second of two things mentioned
